FILED s407 (Fable) â docs/option-b-phase2-plan.md Â§2 Track B1 is the design.
Probed s407: `print -f -d "/tmp" ? â¦` and `-e -f "/etc/passwd"` DROP ("Fell
through"); `defined -e $f`, `!-e $f`, `!!$y`, `- -$y` all work (inverse guards).
The operand-taker (_reduce_term via _term_extent, then _extend_high_prec)
declines a leading prefix op BY DESIGN and the site falls back to the $end_pars
machinery, which has no case for a named unary whose operand is another named
unary.  DESIGN: in the ONE operand-taker, operand := NAMED-UNARY operand | term
high-prec-tail â a named unary / filetest at operand start recurses, producing
the funcall/prefix node that IS the term; precedence is already right (named
unary binds tighter than comparisons, looser than arithmetic; _extend_high_prec
applies to the inner operand as it does today for `ref $x + 1`).
ACCEPTANCE (perl-oracle rows in Pl/t/reduce-term-01.t): -f -d $x; -l -e _;
-e -t -t $tty; -f -d $x ? 1 : 0; -f -d $x && $y; lc -e $f; defined -e $f and
!-e $f as inverses; the comma continuation after the chain (`ok(-f -r $1, "d")`).
POPULATION: t/op/filetest.t 19, filetest_t.t 5, stat.t 2, tie_fetch_count.t 1
stop dropping â rows spliced with causes; census edited.

over the FOUR populations, byte-identical except the explained diffs; then

RE-DESIGNED FROM MEASUREMENT (Fable s416): docs/b1-operand-grammar-s416.md SUPERSEDES the grammar sketch above. The drop is NOT at the operand-taker: _default_filetest_operand consults _is_print_term_start, which answers 0 for a -X Operator, so $_ is spliced mid-run. The operator loop already reduces prefix runs rightmost-first. B1 = (1) one predicate line (a -[A-Za-z] Operator starts a term) + the print-argument leg it exposes (print $fh -e X mis-lowers to a call of sub e â fix or die in the same commit); (2) the stacked-run LOWERING desugars to the _-chain (-f -d $x == -d $x && -f _, short-circuit) â naive nesting (p--f (p--d $x)) is SILENT WRONG, probed (-e -f /etc/passwd: perl 1, nest undef); (3) census/baseline edits. NO _term_extent change, NO $end_pars edits. Fidelity note: PCL -f _ answers undef where perl answers "" (defined-false) â same-commit if one site. Probe list and A/B recipe in the doc.

=== DONE s417 (Fable) â shipped exactly as docs/b1-operand-grammar-s416.md ===

THREE pieces, one commit:

 1. `_is_print_term_start` answers 1 for a `-[A-Za-z]` Operator.  One line in
    the SHARED oracle, not scoped to the caller that had the bug, because all
    three call sites want perl's answer (probed: `print STDERR -e $f` reads
    STDERR as the handle BECAUSE `-e` starts a term).

 2. The LOWERING: `_filetest_prefix_node` marks each filetest reduction and,
    when an outer filetest finds a marked operand, builds perl's documented
    `_`-chain by RE-PARSING `INNER && -X _` â no new emission case.  The naive
    nest was measured silent-wrong in the opposite direction (`-e -f
    /etc/passwd`: perl 1, nest undef).  A mixed run (`! -e $f`) keeps today's
    per-op recursion; a variable holding a filetest's VALUE does not stack,
    which is what perl does too.

 3. The print-argument leg the predicate exposed, which turned out to be a
    PPI BUG: after a SCALAR or BLOCK filehandle PPI splits `-e` into
    Operator('-') + Word('e'), so `print $fh -e $f` lowered to a subtraction of
    a call to sub `e` and crashed at load.  `_fuse_print_filehandle_filetest`
    re-fuses the tokens when they are ADJACENT (`next_sibling`), which is the
    discriminator perl itself uses (`print $fh - e $f` really IS `-(e($f))`).
    Logged as ppi-upstream-bugs.md Â§22 + three rows in docs/ppi-bug-report.t
    (plan 20 -> 23) + a canary in Pl/t/misc-fixes-02.t (plan 121 -> 122).

NOT done, per Â§5: no `_term_extent`/`_reduce_term` change, no `$end_pars`
edits, no new grammar production, no named-unary WORD-site change.  Nothing
needed them â the operator loop's existing prefix-run walk already reduces the
run rightmost-first.
